sentences.zh: 蕭景先

translations.literal: Xiao Jingxian
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingxian

sentences.zh: 蕭景先，南蘭陵蘭陵人，太祖從子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Jingxian was a man of Lanling in Nan Lanling, a cousin's son of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingxian was a native of Lanling in Nan Lanling, a cousin's son of Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 祖爰之，員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aizhi was Outer Gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Aizhi had served as Outer Gentleman-attendant.

sentences.zh: 父敬宗，始興王國中軍。

translations.literal: His father Jingzong was Central Army of the Principality of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingzong had been Central Army of the Principality of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 景先少遭父喪，有至性，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Jingxian in youth suffered his father's death, had utmost filial nature, and the Grand Progenitor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian lost his father while still young and showed exceptional filial devotion, which Emperor Gao greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 及從官京邑，常相提攜。

translations.literal: When he followed into office in the capital, they were constantly together in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered service in the capital, the emperor kept him close and relied on him constantly.

sentences.zh: 解褐爲海陵王國上軍將軍，補建陵令，還爲新安王國侍郎，桂陽國右常侍。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the cotton garment he became Senior General of the Army of the Principality of Hailing, was appointed Magistrate of Jianling, returned to serve as Gentleman-attendant of the Principality of Xin'an, and Right Regular Attendant of the Principality of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he was made Senior General of the Army of the Principality of Hailing, then Magistrate of Jianling; he later served as Gentleman-attendant of the Principality of Xin'an and as Right Regular Attendant of the Principality of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮淮陰，景先以本官領軍主自隨，防衞城內，委以心腹。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor garrisoned Huaiyin, Jingxian with his existing office led army commanders to follow in person, guarded the city interior, and was entrusted as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao held Huaiyin, Jingxian retained his rank but led troops in the emperor's train, garrisoned the city, and was treated as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 除後軍行參軍，邛縣令，員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Aide of the Rear Army, Magistrate of Qiong County, and Outer Gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Aide of the Rear Army, Magistrate of Qiong County, and Outer Gentleman-attendant.

sentences.zh: 與世祖款暱，世祖爲廣興郡，啓太祖求景先同行，除世祖寧朔府司馬，自此常相隨逐。

translations.literal: He was on warm intimate terms with the Heir Apparent; when the Heir Apparent was at Guangxing commandery he memorialized the Grand Progenitor asking that Jingxian go with him, and Jingxian was appointed Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Pacifying-the-North headquarters; from then on they were constantly together in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was on close, affectionate terms with the future Emperor Wu; when the latter was assigned to Guangxing commandery he asked Emperor Gao to let Jingxian accompany him, and Jingxian was made Marshal of his Pacifying-the-North headquarters. From then on the two were rarely apart.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲鎮西長史，以景先爲鎮西長流參軍，除寧朔將軍，隨府轉撫軍中兵參軍，尋除諮議，領中兵如故。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent was Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters, he made Jingxian Senior Adjutant of the Long Stream of the Pacify-the-West headquarters, appointed him General of Pacifying the North, transferred with the headquarters to become Army Aide of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters, and soon appointed him Adviser while continuing to lead the central army as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor became Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters, he made Jingxian Senior Adjutant on that staff and promoted him to General of Pacifying the North; Jingxian followed the headquarters and became Army Aide on the Pacify-the-Army staff, then Adviser while still commanding the central army.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，爲世祖征虜府司馬，領新蔡太守，隨上鎮盆城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengming era he was Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Subdue-the-Barbarians headquarters, concurrently Administrator of Xincai, and followed him in garrisoning Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengming era he served as Marshal of the heir's Subdue-the-Barbarians headquarters and as Administrator of Xincai, accompanying him to the garrison at Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事平，還都，除寧朔將軍，驍騎將軍，仍爲世祖撫軍中軍二府司馬，兼左衞將軍。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair was settled they returned to the capital; he was appointed General of Pacifying the North and General of Valiant Cavalry, and continued as Marshal of both the Pacify-the-Army and Central Army headquarters of the Heir Apparent, concurrently General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Youzhi's rebellion was crushed they returned to the capital; he was made General of Pacifying the North and General of Valiant Cavalry, and continued as marshal on both the Pacify-the-Army and Central Army staffs of the heir, while also serving as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: ，遷太子左衞率，封新吳縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Baron of Xinwu County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Baron of Xinwu with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 景先本名道先，乃改避上諱。

translations.literal: Jingxian's original name was Daoxian; he then changed it to avoid the imperial taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian had originally been named Daoxian; he changed his name to avoid the imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督司州軍事、寧朔將軍、司州刺史，領義陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Sizhou, General of Pacifying the North, Inspector of Sizhou, and concurrently Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out bearing the staff as Supervisor of Sizhou military affairs, General of Pacifying the North, and Inspector of Sizhou, while also serving as Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 是冬，虜出淮、泗，增司部邊戍兵。

translations.literal: That winter the barbarians came out from the Huai and Si, and border garrison troops in the Sizhou region were increased.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the northerners raided along the Huai and Si, and frontier garrisons in the Sizhou region were reinforced.

sentences.zh: 義陽人謝天蓋與虜相構扇，景先言於督府，驃騎豫章王遣輔國將軍中兵參軍蕭惠朗二千人助景先。

translations.literal: Xie Tiangai of Yiyang colluded with and incited the barbarians; Jingxian reported to the supervisory headquarters, and the General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Yuzhang, sent the Army Aide of the Assistant State, Xiao Huilang, with two thousand men to assist Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiangai of Yiyang conspired with the enemy to stir up trouble; Jingxian reported to headquarters, and the Prince of Yuzhang, General of Agile Cavalry, sent Xiao Huilang, Army Aide of the Assistant State, with two thousand men to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 惠朗依山築城，斷塞關隘，討天蓋黨與。

translations.literal: Huilang built a fortress against the mountains, blocked and sealed the passes, and attacked Tiangai's partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Huilang built a mountain fortress, sealed the passes, and hunted down Tiangai's accomplices.

sentences.zh: 虜尋遣偽南部尚書頞跋屯汝南，洛州刺史昌黎王馮莎屯清丘。

translations.literal: The barbarians soon sent the false Minister of the Southern Department Eba to encamp at Runan, and the Prince of Changli, Feng Sha, Governor of Luozhou, to encamp at Qingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon sent their Minister of the Southern Department Eba to camp at Runan and the Prince of Changli, Feng Sha, Governor of Luozhou, to camp at Qingqiu.

sentences.zh: 景先嚴備待敵。

translations.literal: Jingxian made strict preparations and awaited the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian made thorough preparations and stood ready for battle.

sentences.zh: 豫章王又遣寧朔將軍王僧炳、前軍將軍王應之、龍驤將軍莊明三千人屯義陽關外，爲聲援。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang again sent General of Pacifying the North Wang Bingbing, General of the Van Wang Yingzhi, and General of the Flying Dragon Zhuang Ming with three thousand men to encamp outside the Yiyang Pass as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang also sent Wang Bingbing, General of Pacifying the North, Wang Yingzhi, General of the Van, and Zhuang Ming, General of the Flying Dragon, with three thousand men to camp outside Yiyang Pass as a reserve force.

sentences.zh: 虜退，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, his title was advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, his rank was raised to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 景先啓稱上德化之美。

translations.literal: Jingxian in a memorial praised the emperor's virtue and transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian submitted a memorial praising the emperor's moral influence and civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 上答曰：「風淪俗敗，二十餘年，以吾當之，豈得頓掃。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "Customs have collapsed and morals ruined for more than twenty years; with me to bear it, how could it be swept clean at once?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "For more than twenty years customs have decayed and morals have collapsed. With me to answer for it, how could all that be swept away at once?

sentences.zh: 幸得數載盡力救蒼生者，必有功於萬物也。

translations.literal: If fortunately for several years I can exert my strength to rescue the black-haired people, there will surely be merit toward the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: If in a few years I can devote myself fully to saving the people, I shall have done some good for the world.

sentences.zh: 治天下者，雖聖人猶須良佐，汝等各各自竭，不憂不治也。」

translations.literal: One who governs All-under-Heaven, even a sage, still needs good assistants; you and the rest each exhaust yourselves—there is no worry that it will not be well governed."
translations.idiomatic: Even a sage who rules the realm still needs able helpers. Each of you must give your utmost, and then there is no reason to fear that the realm will not be well governed."

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，徵爲侍中，領左軍將軍，尋兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent ascended the throne, Jingxian was summoned as Palace Attendant and concurrently General of the Left Army, and soon also concurrently General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Jingxian was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant and General of the Left Army, and soon also as General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 景先事上盡心，故恩寵特密。

translations.literal: Jingxian served the emperor with full devotion, and therefore favor and grace were especially close.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian served the emperor with complete devotion, and for that reason enjoyed especially intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 初西還，上坐景陽樓召景先語故舊，唯豫章王一人在席而已。

translations.literal: When he first returned from the west, the emperor sat on Jingyang Tower and summoned Jingxian to speak of old times; only the Prince of Yuzhang was at the seat besides them.
translations.idiomatic: When he first returned from the west, the emperor received him on Jingyang Tower to talk over old times; apart from the emperor and Jingxian, only the Prince of Yuzhang was present.

sentences.zh: 轉中領軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Central General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 車駕射雉郊外行游，景先常甲仗從，廉察左右。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage shot pheasants on excursions outside the suburbs, Jingxian constantly followed in armor with weapons and inspected those to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out to the suburbs to hunt pheasants, Jingxian always followed in armor on guard and kept watch over those around him.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵爲侯。

translations.literal: Soon his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his noble rank was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 領太子詹事，本官如故。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Steward of the Heir Apparent's household, his original offices remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent's household while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，詔超起爲領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When he encountered his mother's mourning, an edict ordered him to rise before the mourning period ended and serve as General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, an edict recalled him from mourning to serve again as General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，荒人桓天生引蠻虜於雍州界上，司部以北，人情騷動。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the wild man Huan Tiansheng led Man barbarians and northern invaders on the borders of Yongzhou; north of the Sizhou region popular feeling was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the outlaw Huan Tiansheng led tribal and northern forces on the Yongzhou frontier, and north of the Sizhou region the people were thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 上以景先諳究司土，詔曰：「得雍州刺史張瓌啓事，蠻虜相扇，容或侵軼。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Jingxian thoroughly versed in the lands of Sizhou, an edict said: "We have received a memorial from Zhang Gui, Inspector of Yongzhou, that the Man and the invaders are inciting one another and may perhaps raid and harass.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor knew Jingxian was thoroughly familiar with the Sizhou region, he issued an edict: "We have received a report from Zhang Gui, Inspector of Yongzhou, that tribal and northern forces are stirring one another up and may raid our borders.

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆有毒，宜時剿蕩。

translations.literal: Wasps and scorpions have poison; they should be exterminated at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Even small poisons must be dealt with in time; they should be crushed promptly.

sentences.zh: 可遣征虜將軍丹陽尹景先總率步騎，直指義陽。

translations.literal: General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Intendant of Danyang Jingxian may be sent to command infantry and cavalry in total and strike directly at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Let General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Intendant of Danyang Jingxian take overall command of infantry and cavalry and march straight on Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 可假節，司州諸軍皆受節度。

translations.literal: He may be lent the staff; all armies of Sizhou shall receive his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him the staff of authority; all armies in Sizhou shall come under his command.

sentences.zh: 」景先至鎮，屯軍城北，百姓乃安，牛酒來迎。

translations.literal: " When Jingxian reached his post he encamped his army north of the city, the common people were then at peace, and cattle and wine were brought to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Jingxian reached his post he encamped north of the city; the people were reassured, and they came bringing cattle and wine to welcome his troops.

sentences.zh: 軍未還，遇疾，遺言曰：「此度疾病，異於前後，自省必無起理。

translations.literal: Before the army returned he fell ill; his final words said: "This bout of illness differs from those before and after; examining myself, there is surely no prospect of rising.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army could return he fell ill. His final instructions read: "This illness is unlike any I have had before; I know I shall not recover.

sentences.zh: 但夙荷深恩，今謬充戎寄，闇弱每事不稱，上慚慈旨。

translations.literal: Yet long bearing deep grace, now wrongly filling a military post, dim and weak in every matter not matching, above I am ashamed before the compassionate edicts.
translations.idiomatic: I have long owed the deepest grace, yet now I have been wrongly placed in command of troops; feeble and incompetent, I have failed in every task and am ashamed before your kindness.

sentences.zh: 便長違聖世，悲哽不知所言。

translations.literal: I shall soon long depart the sage age; grief and choking leave me not knowing what to say.
translations.idiomatic: I must soon leave this enlightened age forever, and grief chokes me beyond words.

sentences.zh: 可爲作啓事，上謝至尊，粗申愚心。

translations.literal: You may draft a memorial for me, above thanking the Supreme One, roughly declaring my foolish heart.
translations.idiomatic: Please draft a memorial for me to thank His Majesty and express, however roughly, what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 毅雖成長，素闕訓範。

translations.literal: Yi though grown to maturity has always lacked instruction and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yi is grown, he has never been properly trained.

sentences.zh: 貞等幼稚，未有所識。

translations.literal: Zhen and the others are young and childish and understand nothing yet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and the others are still children and know nothing.

sentences.zh: 方以仰累聖明，非殘息所能陳謝。

translations.literal: They will rely on the sagely brilliance above; this dying breath cannot declare thanks.
translations.idiomatic: They must now rely entirely on your sage care; these last breaths of mine cannot thank you as I ought.

sentences.zh: 自丁荼毒以來，妓妾已多分張，所餘醜猥數人，皆不似事。

translations.literal: Since encountering bitter poison, singing-girls and concubines have already been largely divided and allotted; the few remaining, ugly and base, are none fit for service.
translations.idiomatic: Since this affliction began, most of my singing-girls and concubines have already been disposed of; the few ugly and worthless ones left are fit for nothing.

sentences.zh: 可以明月、佛女、桂支、佛兒、玉女、美玉上臺，美滿、豔華奉東宮。

translations.literal: Mingyue, Fonü, Guizhi, Fo'er, Yunü, and Meiyu may be sent up to the palace; Meiman and Yanhua may be presented to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Send Mingyue, Fonü, Guizhi, Fo'er, Yunü, and Meiyu to the palace; present Meiman and Yanhua to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 私馬有二十餘匹，牛數頭，可簡好者十匹、牛二頭上臺，馬五匹、牛一頭奉東宮，大司馬、司徒各奉二匹，驃騎、鎮軍各奉一匹。

translations.literal: Private horses number more than twenty head and cattle several head; select the good ones—ten horses and two cattle to the palace, five horses and one ox to the Eastern Palace, two each to the Grand Marshal and Minister Over the Masses, one each to the General of Agile Cavalry and the General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: I have more than twenty private horses and several oxen; choose the best—ten horses and two oxen for the palace, five horses and one ox for the Eastern Palace, two horses each for the Grand Marshal and Minister Over the Masses, and one each for the General of Agile Cavalry and the General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 應私仗器，亦悉輸臺。

translations.literal: Private weapons and gear that should be surrendered shall all be delivered to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: All private arms and equipment should likewise be sent to the palace.

sentences.zh: 六親多未得料理，可隨宜溫卹，微申素意。

translations.literal: Many among the six relations have not yet been provided for; you may as appropriate comfort and relieve them, slightly expressing my long-standing intent.
translations.idiomatic: Many of my kin remain unsettled; comfort them as you see fit and let them know something of my wishes.

sentences.zh: 所賜宅曠大，恐非毅等所居，須喪服竟，可輸還臺。

translations.literal: The residence bestowed is vast and large; I fear it is not where Yi and the others should dwell; when mourning garments are finished it may be returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The house I was granted is too large for Yi and the others; when mourning is over, return it to the palace.

sentences.zh: 劉家前宅，久聞其貨，可合率市之，直若短少，啓官乞足。

translations.literal: The Liu family's former residence—I have long heard it is for sale; you may jointly arrange to buy it at market; if the price falls short, memorialize the authorities to make it up.
translations.idiomatic: I have long heard that the Liu family's former house is for sale; arrange to buy it together, and if the price is short, ask the authorities to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 三處田勤，作自足供，衣食力少，更隨宜買麤猥奴婢充使。

translations.literal: The three plots of fields are diligently worked and can supply sufficiency; for clothing and food the labor force is small—further, as appropriate buy coarse and base slave boys and girls to fill service.
translations.idiomatic: The income from my three estates should suffice for daily needs; if hands are few for food and clothing, buy such coarse servants as may be needed.

sentences.zh: 不須餘營生。

translations.literal: There is no need for further livelihood enterprises.
translations.idiomatic: They need seek no other livelihood.

sentences.zh: 周旋部曲還都，理應分張，其久舊勞勤者，應料理，隨宜啓聞乞恩。

translations.literal: The retainers who have attended me, on returning to the capital, should by right be divided and allotted; those long in service and laborious should be provided for, and as appropriate report and beg grace.
translations.idiomatic: My household retainers who return to the capital should be settled according to custom; those of long and faithful service should be cared for, and you may memorialize on their behalf for imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 」卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: " He died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: " He died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 上傷惜之，詔曰：「西信適至，景先奄至喪逝，悲懷切割，自不勝任。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved and cherished his memory; an edict said: "News from the west has just arrived that Jingxian has suddenly reached mourning and death; grief cuts to the heart and I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and issued an edict: "Word has just come from the west that Jingxian has suddenly died. My grief is unbearable.

sentences.zh: 今便舉哀。

translations.literal: Let mourning be raised at once.
translations.idiomatic: Let mourning be proclaimed immediately.

sentences.zh: 賻錢十萬，布二百匹。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts: one hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Grant funeral gifts of one hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 」景先喪還，詔曰：「故假節征虜將軍丹陽尹新吳侯景先，器懷開亮，幹局通敏。

translations.literal: " When Jingxian's coffin returned, an edict said: "The late Bearer of the Staff, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Intendant of Danyang, and Marquis of Xinwu Jingxian had capacity and breast open and bright, administrative framework penetrating and keen.
translations.idiomatic: " When Jingxian's coffin returned, an edict said: "The late Bearer of the Staff, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Intendant of Danyang, and Marquis of Xinwu Jingxian was open and bright in character and quick and capable in affairs.

sentences.zh: 綢繆少長，義兼勳戚。

translations.literal: From youth to age he was bound close; in righteousness he combined merit and kinship.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age we were bound in close friendship, united by both merit and kinship.

sentences.zh: 誠著夷險，績茂所司。

translations.literal: Loyalty showed in calm and danger; achievements flourished in what he oversaw.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty stood firm through easy times and hard, and his achievements in office were outstanding.

sentences.zh: 方升寵榮，用申任寄。

translations.literal: Just as he was to rise in favor and glory, to extend the trust placed in him—
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of greater honors, to which I had intended to entrust him further—

sentences.zh: 奄至喪逝，悲痛良深。

translations.literal: suddenly he reached mourning and death; grief is truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: when suddenly he died. My grief is profound.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、征北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns North, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns North, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Grant one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Grant one band of martial music.

sentences.zh: 假節、侯如故。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff and marquisate remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: His staff of authority and marquisate shall remain as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠侯。」

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Loyal Marquis."
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title shall be Loyal Marquis."

sentences.zh: 子毅，以勳戚子，少歷清官。

translations.literal: His son Yi, as son of a meritorious kinsman, in youth passed through pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, as the son of a meritorious kinsman, early held respectable posts.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人，洗馬，隨王友，永嘉太守，大司馬諮議參軍，南康太守，中書郎。

translations.literal: Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, Friend of the Prince of Sui, Administrator of Yongjia, Adviser of the Grand Marshal, Administrator of Nankang, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, Friend of the Prince of Sui, Administrator of Yongjia, Adviser on the staff of the Grand Marshal, Administrator of Nankang, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建武初，爲撫軍司馬，遷北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was Marshal of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters and was transferred to Marshal of the North Central Commandant headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was Marshal of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters, then Marshal of the North Central Commandant headquarters.

sentences.zh: 虜動，領軍守琅邪城。

translations.literal: When the barbarians stirred, he led the army in defending Langye city.
translations.idiomatic: When the northerners moved, he commanded troops in the defense of Langye.

sentences.zh: 毅性奢豪，好弓馬，爲高宗所疑忌。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was extravagant and proud; he loved bow and horse and was suspected and envied by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was extravagant by nature and loved archery and horsemanship; Emperor Ming came to view him with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 王晏事敗，幷陷誅之。

translations.literal: When Wang Yan's affair failed, Yi was implicated and executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan's plot failed, Yi was implicated and executed along with him.

sentences.zh: 遣軍圍宅，毅時會賔客奏伎，聞變，索刀未得，收人突進，挾持毅入與母別，出便殺之。

translations.literal: Troops were sent to surround the residence; Yi at the time was hosting guests with performers playing; hearing the change, he sought a knife but did not obtain it; arresters burst in, seized Yi and brought him in to part from his mother, and once outside killed him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were sent to surround his house while he was entertaining guests with music. When he heard what was happening he reached for a knife but could not find one; the arresters burst in, took him in to bid his mother farewell, and killed him as soon as they led him out.

sentences.zh: 蕭赤斧

translations.literal: Xiao Chifu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chifu

sentences.zh: 蕭赤斧，南蘭陵人，太祖從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Xiao Chifu was a man of Nan Lanling, a cousin's younger brother of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chifu was a native of Nan Lanling, a younger cousin of Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 祖隆子，衞軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Longzi was Recorder-aide of the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Longzi had been Recorder-aide on the staff of the Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 父始之，冠軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His father Shizhi was Army Aide of the Champion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shizhi had been Army Aide on the staff of the Champion.

sentences.zh: 赤斧歷官爲奉朝請，以和謹爲太祖所知。

translations.literal: Chifu through his offices was Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, and through harmony and prudence was known to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Chifu served as Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences and became known to Emperor Gao for his mild and careful character.

sentences.zh: 宋大明初，竟陵王誕反廣陵，赤斧爲軍主，隷沈慶之，圍廣陵城，攻戰有勳，事寧，封永安亭侯，食邑三百七十戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song Daming era, Prince of Jingling Dan rebelled at Guangling; Chifu was army commander, subordinate to Shen Qingzhi, besieged Guangling city, and in attack and battle had merit; when the affair was settled he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an village with a fief of three hundred seventy households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song Daming era, when Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled at Guangling, Chifu served as army commander under Shen Qingzhi, besieged the city, and distinguished himself in the fighting. When the rebellion was crushed he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an village with a fief of three hundred seventy households.

sentences.zh: 除車騎行參軍，出補晉陵令，員外郎，丹楊令，還除晉熙王撫軍中兵參軍，出爲建威將軍、錢唐令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Aide of the Chariots and Cavalry, went out to fill the post of Magistrate of Jinling, Outer Gentleman-attendant, Magistrate of Danyang, returned and was appointed Army Aide of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters of the Prince of Jinxi, and went out as General Who Establishes Might and Magistrate of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Aide of the Chariots and Cavalry, then Magistrate of Jinling, Outer Gentleman-attendant, and Magistrate of Danyang; he later became Army Aide on the Pacify-the-Army staff of the Prince of Jinxi, then General Who Establishes Might and Magistrate of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 遷正員郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 赤斧治政爲百姓所安，吏民請留之，時議見許，改除寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Chifu's governance in administration made the common people secure; officials and people asked that he be retained, contemporary opinion approved, and his appointment was changed to General of Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: Chifu's administration won the people's trust; officials and commoners petitioned to keep him, the court agreed, and he was reappointed General of Pacifying the North.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，以赤斧爲輔國將軍、左軍會稽司馬，輔鎮東境。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor assisted in government, he made Chifu General Who Assists the State and Left Army Kuaiji Marshal, assisting in garrisoning the eastern marches.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao held the regency he appointed Chifu General Who Assists the State and Left Army Kuaiji Marshal to help secure the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎，淮陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 從帝遜位，於丹陽故治立宮，上令赤斧輔送，至薨乃還。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor yielded the throne, a palace was established at the old seat of Danyang; the emperor ordered Chifu to assist in escorting him, and he returned only when the deposed emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor abdicated, a residence was set up at the old Danyang seat; the emperor ordered Chifu to assist in escorting him and Chifu returned only after the former emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 建元初，遷武陵王冠軍長史，驃騎司馬，南東海太守，輔國將軍竝如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Champion of the Prince of Wuling, Marshal of the General of Agile Cavalry, Administrator of South Donghai, and General Who Assists the State, all concurrently as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era he became Chief Clerk of the Champion on the staff of the Prince of Wuling, Marshal of the General of Agile Cavalry, and Administrator of South Donghai, while retaining his rank as General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 遷長兼侍中，祖母喪去職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Concurrent Palace Attendant and left office for his grandmother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Concurrent Palace Attendant, then left office to mourn his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 起爲冠軍將軍、寧蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He was raised from mourning as General of the Champion and Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning as General of the Champion and Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、雍州刺史，本官如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces Yong, Liang, North Qin, and South Qin, Jingling in Jingzhou and Suizhou in Sizhou, Inspector of Yongzhou, his original offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out bearing the staff as Supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North Qin, and South Qin, in Jingling of Jingzhou and Suizhou of Sizhou, and as Inspector of Yongzhou, while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 在州不營產利，勤於奉公。

translations.literal: In the province he did not pursue property and profit but was diligent in serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he sought no private gain and devoted himself diligently to public duty.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，左衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 世祖親遇與蕭景先相比。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent treated him with personal favor comparable to Xiao Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu favored him personally in a manner comparable to Xiao Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 封南豐縣伯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanfeng County with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanfeng with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Within the Gates and Steward of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Within the Gates and Steward of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 赤斧夙患渴利，會，世祖使甲仗衞三廂，赤斧不敢辭，疾甚，數日卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: Chifu had long suffered from wasting thirst; on one occasion the Heir Apparent ordered armored guards for three wings of the palace, and Chifu dared not decline; his illness grew severe and within several days he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Chifu had long suffered from a wasting illness with severe thirst. When Emperor Wu ordered armored guards for three palace wings, Chifu did not dare refuse; his condition worsened and he died within days, at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 家無儲積，無絹爲衾，上聞之，愈加惋惜。

translations.literal: The family had no stored wealth and no silk for a quilt; when the emperor heard of it his regret and cherishing increased still more.
translations.idiomatic: The household had no savings and not even silk for a burial quilt; when the emperor learned of this his grief deepened.

sentences.zh: 詔賻錢五萬，上材一具，布百匹，蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: An edict granted funeral gifts of fifty thousand cash, one set of superior timber, one hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted fifty thousand cash in funeral gifts, one set of superior coffin timber, one hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 諡曰懿伯。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Reverent Baron.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Reverent Baron.

sentences.zh: 子穎冑襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yingzhou inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yingzhou inherited the title.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎冑

translations.literal: Xiao Yingzhou
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingzhou

sentences.zh: =穎冑字雲長，弘厚有父風。

translations.literal: = Yingzhou styled Yunchang; he was broad and substantial and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou, styled Yunchang, was magnanimous and steady, with his father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂赤斧曰：「穎冑輕朱被身，覺其趨進轉美，足慰人意。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to Chifu: "Yingzhou lightly wears vermilion upon his person; I find his bearing in advancing ever more fine—it fully comforts the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said to Chifu: "Yingzhou wears vermilion so lightly upon him; his bearing as he advances grows ever finer—it is truly a comfort to behold.

sentences.zh: 」遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then appointed Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，感脚疾，數年然後能行。

translations.literal: When he encountered his father's mourning he was afflicted with foot illness and only after several years could he walk.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was stricken with a foot ailment and could walk again only after several years.

sentences.zh: 世祖有詔慰勉，賜醫藥。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent issued an edict of consolation and encouragement and bestowed medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu issued an edict of consolation and bestowed medicines.

sentences.zh: 除竟陵王司徒外兵參軍，晉熙王文學。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Army Aide on the staff of the Prince of Jingling's Minister Over the Masses, and Literary Scholar of the Prince of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Outer Army Aide on the staff of the Prince of Jingling's Minister Over the Masses and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 穎冑好文義，弟穎基好武勇，世祖登烽火樓，詔羣臣賦詩。

translations.literal: Yingzhou loved literary meaning; his younger brother Yingji loved martial valor. The Heir Apparent ascended the Beacon Fire Tower and ordered the assembled ministers to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou loved literature; his younger brother Yingji loved martial arts. Emperor Wu ascended the Beacon Fire Tower and ordered the ministers to compose poems.

sentences.zh: 穎冑詩合旨，上謂穎冑曰：「卿文弟武，宗室便不乏才。

translations.literal: Yingzhou's poem matched the intent; the emperor said to Yingzhou: "You are the literary brother and he the martial—among the imperial clan we shall not lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou's poem pleased the emperor, who said to him: "One brother literary, one martial—the imperial house will not want for talent.

sentences.zh: 」除明威將軍、安陸內史。

translations.literal: " He was appointed General of Illustrious Might and Administrator of the Interior of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed General of Illustrious Might and Interior Administrator of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上以穎冑勳戚子弟，除左將軍，知殿內文武事，得入便殿。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Yingzhou a son of meritorious kin, he appointed him General of the Left to manage civil and military affairs within the palace halls, with permission to enter the informal audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yingzhou was the son of a meritorious kinsman, the emperor made him General of the Left to oversee civil and military affairs in the palace and allowed him entry to the informal audience hall.

sentences.zh: 出爲新安太守，吏民懷之。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xin'an; officials and commoners cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Xin'an he won the loyalty of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: ，永嘉王昭粲爲南徐州，以穎冑爲南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhaocan of Yongjia was assigned to South Xuzhou, Yingzhou was made Administrator of South Donghai and acted in South Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhaocan of Yongjia was assigned to South Xuzhou, Yingzhou became Administrator of South Donghai and handled South Xuzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉持節、督青冀二州軍事、輔國將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Qing and Ji military affairs, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 不行，除黃門郎，領四廂直。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post and was instead appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, commanding the four palace guard wings on duty.
translations.idiomatic: He declined that appointment and was made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, commanding the four palace guard wings on duty.

sentences.zh: 遷衞尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commandant of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 高宗廢立，穎冑從容不爲同異，乃引穎冑預功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming deposed and enthroned emperors, Yingzhou was composed and made no show of agreement or dissent; therefore the emperor drew him in to share in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming carried out his depositions and enthronements, Yingzhou remained outwardly unmoved; the emperor therefore counted him among those who had aided the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，進爵侯，增邑爲六百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu his noble rank was advanced to marquis and his fief increased to six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he was raised to marquis and his fief increased to six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 賜穎冑以常所乘白＜牜俞＞牛。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Yingzhou the white riding ox he habitually used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Yingzhou the white ox he habitually rode.

sentences.zh: 上慕儉約，欲鑄壞太官元日上壽銀酒鎗，尚書令王晏等咸稱盛德。

translations.literal: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Minister Over the Masses Wang Yan and others all praised this as supreme virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Wang Yan, Minister Over the Masses, and others all praised this as supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 穎冑曰：「朝廷盛禮，莫過三元。

translations.literal: Yingzhou said: "Among the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou said: "Of all the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.

sentences.zh: 此一器旣是舊物，不足爲侈。

translations.literal: This single vessel is already an old object and is not enough to count as extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: This one vessel is an heirloom and hardly counts as extravagance.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後預曲宴，銀器滿席。

translations.literal: Later, at a private banquet, silver vessels filled the mats.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an informal banquet, silver vessels covered the tables.

sentences.zh: 穎冑曰：「陛下前欲壞酒鎗，恐宜移在此器也。

translations.literal: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty formerly wished to destroy the wine ladle—I fear the effort should have been directed at these vessels instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty once wished to destroy the wine ladle—perhaps the effort should have been directed at these vessels instead.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚有慚色。

translations.literal: " The emperor was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 冠軍江夏王寶玄鎮石頭，以穎冑爲長史，行石頭戍事。

translations.literal: When the Champion Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia garrisoned Stone City, Yingzhou was made his Chief Clerk and acted in Stone City garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia, the Champion, garrisoned Stone City, Yingzhou became his Chief Clerk and handled the garrison affairs.

sentences.zh: 復爲衞尉。

translations.literal: He again served as Commandant of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Commandant of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 出爲冠軍將軍、廬陵王後軍長史、廣陵太守、行南兖州府州事。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Champion, Chief Clerk of the Rear Army of the Prince of Luling, Administrator of Guangling, and acting in South Yanzhou headquarters and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General of the Champion, Chief Clerk of the Rear Army on the staff of the Prince of Luling, Administrator of Guangling, and acting head of South Yanzhou headquarters and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 是年虜動，揚聲當飲馬長江。

translations.literal: That year the barbarians stirred; they proclaimed they would water their horses in the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: That year the northerners raided, boasting they would water their horses in the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，敕穎冑移居民入城，百姓驚恐，席卷欲南渡。

translations.literal: The emperor was afraid and ordered Yingzhou to move residents into the city; the common people were terrified and swept along in a rush to flee south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and ordered Yingzhou to move the population into the city; the people panicked and surged southward to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 穎冑以賊勢尚遠，不卽施行，虜亦尋退。

translations.literal: Yingzhou considered the enemy's strength still distant and did not immediately carry it out; the barbarians also soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou judged the enemy still distant and did not act at once; the raiders soon withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 仍爲持節、督南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、輔國將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: He then served as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 和帝爲荊州，以穎冑爲冠軍將軍、西中郎長史、南郡太守、行荊州府、州事。

translations.literal: When Prince He of Jing was assigned to Jingzhou, Yingzhou was made General of the Champion, Chief Clerk of the West Central Commandant, Administrator of Nan commandery, and acting in Jingzhou headquarters and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince He of Jing was assigned to Jingzhou, Yingzhou became General of the Champion, Chief Clerk of the West Central Commandant, Administrator of Nan commandery, and acting head of Jingzhou headquarters and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯誅戮羣公，委任廝小，崔、陳敗後，方鎮各懷異計。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Donghun executed the great ministers and entrusted power to base menial attendants; after the defeats of Cui and Chen, each regional commander harbored separate designs.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Donghun slaughtered the leading ministers and entrusted power to base attendants; after the defeats of Cui Huijing and Chen Zande, each regional commander nursed his own designs.

sentences.zh: 永元二年十月，尚書令臨湘侯蕭懿及弟衞尉暢見害，先遣輔國將軍、巴西梓潼二郡太守劉山陽領三千兵受旨之官，就穎冑共襲雍州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Yongyuan, Minister Over the Masses Xiao Yi of Linxiang and his younger brother the Commandant of the Palace Guards Chang were killed; earlier the court had first sent General Who Assists the State Liu Shanyang, concurrently Administrator of Baxi and Zitong, with three thousand troops under imperial orders to take up his post and join Yingzhou in a joint strike on Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Yongyuan, Xiao Yi of Linxiang, Minister Over the Masses, and his younger brother Chang, Commandant of the Palace Guards, were killed. The court had already sent Liu Shanyang, General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Baxi and Zitong, with three thousand men under imperial orders to take up his post and join Yingzhou in attacking Yong province.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史梁王將起義兵，慮穎冑不識機變，遣使王天虎詣江陵，聲云山陽西上，竝襲荊、雍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang was about to raise an army of righteousness and feared Yingzhou would not recognize the turning moment; he sent the envoy Wang Tianhu to Jiangling, proclaiming that Shanyang was marching west and would attack Jing and Yong together.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang was about to raise a righteous army and feared Yingzhou would not seize the moment; he sent Wang Tianhu to Jiangling, claiming that Shanyang was marching west to attack Jing and Yong together.

sentences.zh: 書與穎冑，勸同義舉。

translations.literal: He wrote to Yingzhou urging a joint righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Yingzhou urging him to join the righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 穎冑意猶未決。

translations.literal: Yingzhou's mind was still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 初，山陽出南州，謂人曰：「朝廷以白虎幡追我，亦不復還矣。

translations.literal: At first, when Shanyang left the southern province, he told people: "The court is pursuing me with the white-tiger banner—I shall not return.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang first left the southern province he told people: "The court is pursuing me with the white-tiger banner—I shall not return.

sentences.zh: 」席卷妓妾，盡室而行。

translations.literal: " He swept up singing-girls and concubines and went with his entire household.
translations.idiomatic: " He swept up his singing-girls and concubines and took his whole household with him.

sentences.zh: 至巴陵，遲回十餘日不進。

translations.literal: Reaching Baling he lingered more than ten days without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: At Baling he lingered more than ten days without advancing.

sentences.zh: 梁王復遣天虎馳書與穎冑，陳設其略。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang again sent Tianhu with urgent dispatches to Yingzhou, setting forth the plan in outline.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang again sent Tianhu with urgent dispatches to Yingzhou, outlining the plan.

sentences.zh: 是時或云山陽謀殺穎冑，以荊州同義舉，穎冑乃與梁王定契，斬王天虎首，送示山陽。

translations.literal: At that time some said Shanyang plotted to kill Yingzhou so that Jingzhou might join the righteous rising together; Yingzhou then made a pact with the Prince of Liang, beheaded Wang Tianhu, and sent the head to show Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Some then said Shanyang planned to kill Yingzhou so Jingzhou could join the rising; Yingzhou made a pact with the Prince of Liang, beheaded Wang Tianhu, and sent the head to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 發百姓車牛，聲云起步軍征襄陽。

translations.literal: He mobilized the people's carts and oxen, proclaiming publicly that he was setting out with the army to campaign against Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized civilian carts and oxen, publicly announcing that his army was marching against Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月十八日，山陽至江津，單車白服，從左右數十人，詣穎冑，穎冑使前汶陽太守劉孝慶、前永平太守劉熙曅、鎧曹參軍蕭文照、前建威將軍陳秀、輔國將軍孫末伏兵城內。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the eleventh month Shanyang reached Jiangjin; in a single cart and white garments, with only several tens of attendants at his side, he came to Yingzhou. Yingzhou stationed the former Administrator of Wenyang Liu Xiaoqing, the former Administrator of Yongping Liu Xizhou, Armor Bureau Aide Xiao Wenzhao, the former General Who Establishes Might Chen Xiu, and General Who Assists the State Sun Mo in ambush within the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth of the eleventh month Shanyang reached Jiangjin. In a single cart, dressed in white, with only a few dozen attendants, he came to Yingzhou. Yingzhou had Liu Xiaoqing, former Administrator of Wenyang, Liu Xizhou, former Administrator of Yongping, Xiao Wenzhao, Armor Bureau Aide, Chen Xiu, former General Who Establishes Might, and Sun Mo, General Who Assists the State, lie in ambush inside the city.

sentences.zh: 山陽入門，卽於車中亂斬之。

translations.literal: When Shanyang entered the gate he was hacked to death at once in the cart.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Shanyang entered the gate he was hacked to death in his cart.

sentences.zh: 副軍主李元履收餘衆歸附。

translations.literal: The deputy army commander Li Yuanyi gathered the remaining troops and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy army commander Li Yuanyi gathered the remaining troops and submitted.

sentences.zh: 遣使蔡道猷馳驛送山陽首於梁王，乃發教纂嚴，分部購募。

translations.literal: He sent the envoy Cai Daoyou by post-horse relay to deliver Shanyang's head to the Prince of Liang, then issued an order to gather troops and divided departments to recruit and enlist.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cai Daoyou by relay horse with Shanyang's head to the Prince of Liang, then issued orders to gather troops and opened recruitment in every department.

sentences.zh: 東昏聞山陽死，發詔討荊、雍。

translations.literal: When Donghun heard Shanyang was dead he issued an edict to campaign against Jing and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Donghun learned Shanyang was dead he issued an edict to campaign against Jing and Yong.

sentences.zh: 贈山陽寧朔將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Shanyang was posthumously granted General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang was posthumously made General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 穎冑有器局，旣唱大事，虛心委己，衆情歸之。

translations.literal: Yingzhou had capacity and vision; once he raised the great affair he emptied himself in trust and all hearts turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou had breadth of vision; once the great enterprise was launched he yielded himself in trust and all hearts turned to him.

sentences.zh: 加穎冑右將軍，都督行留諸軍事，置佐史，本官如故。

translations.literal: Yingzhou was additionally made General of the Right, Supervisor of armies remaining and on campaign, with staff officers appointed; his original offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou was further made General of the Right and Supervisor of armies on campaign and in garrison, with staff officers appointed, while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 西中郎司馬夏侯詳加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xiang, Marshal of the West Central Commandant, was additionally made General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang, Marshal of the West Central Commandant, was also made General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 遣寧朔將軍王法度向巴陵。

translations.literal: General of Pacifying the North Wang Fadu was sent toward Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fadu, General of Pacifying the North, was sent toward Baling.

sentences.zh: 穎冑獻錢二十萬，米千斛，鹽五百斛。

translations.literal: Yingzhou presented twenty thousand cash, a thousand hu of grain, and five hundred hu of salt.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou contributed twenty thousand cash, a thousand hu of grain, and five hundred hu of salt.

sentences.zh: 諮議宗塞、別駕宗夬獻穀二千斛，牛二頭。

translations.literal: Adviser Zong Sai and Assisting Officer Zong Jue presented two thousand hu of grain and two head of cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Adviser Zong Sai and Assisting Officer Zong Jue presented two thousand hu of grain and two oxen.

sentences.zh: 換借富貲，以助軍費。

translations.literal: They borrowed from the wealthy to assist military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: They borrowed from wealthy families to help meet military expenses.

sentences.zh: 長沙寺僧業富，沃鑄黃金爲龍數千兩，埋土中，歷相傳付，稱爲下方黃鐵，莫有見者，乃取此龍，以充軍實。

translations.literal: The monk Ye Fu of Changsha Temple was rich; he had molten gold cast into several thousand taels of dragons and buried them in the earth, handed down through generations and called the subterranean yellow iron—none had seen them—yet these dragons were taken to fill military stores.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Ye Fu of Changsha Temple was wealthy; he had gold cast into thousands of taels shaped as dragons and buried in the earth, handed down through generations as "subterranean yellow iron," which none had ever seen. These were now taken to fill the military chest.

sentences.zh: 十二月，移檄：

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he issued a proclamation:
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: :　　西中郎府長史、都督行留諸軍事、右軍將軍、南郡太守、南豐縣開國侯蕭穎冑，司馬、征虜將軍、新興太守夏侯詳告京邑百官，諸州郡牧守：

translations.literal: : Chief Clerk of the West Central Commandant headquarters, Supervisor of armies remaining and on campaign, General of the Right, Administrator of Nan commandery, and Opening Marquis of Nanfeng County Xiao Yingzhou, and Marshal, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Administrator of Xinxing Xiahou Xiang announce to the officials of the capital and to the governors and prefects of all provinces and commanderies:
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Clerk of the West Central Commandant headquarters, Supervisor of armies remaining and on campaign, General of the Right, Administrator of Nan commandery, and Opening Marquis of Nanfeng Xiao Yingzhou, and the Marshal, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Administrator of Xinxing Xiahou Xiang, announce to the officials of the capital and to the governors and prefects of all provinces and commanderies:

sentences.zh: :　　夫運不常夷，有時而陂；

translations.literal: : Fortune does not forever stay level; there are times when it turns steep.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune does not forever stay level; there are times when it turns steep.

sentences.zh: 數無恒剝，否極則亨。

translations.literal: Fate has no fixed decline; when obstruction reaches its limit, flourishing follows.
translations.idiomatic: When decline reaches its limit, flourishing follows.

sentences.zh: 昔商邑中微，彭、韋投袂；

translations.literal: Of old when the Shang capital fell into decline, Peng and Wei cast aside their sleeves;
translations.idiomatic: Of old, when the Shang capital fell into decline, Peng and Wei cast aside their sleeves;

sentences.zh: 漢室方昏，虛、牟效節。

translations.literal: when the Han house was benighted, Xu and Mou showed forth their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: when the Han house was benighted, Xu and Mou showed forth their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故風聲永樹，卜世長久者也。

translations.literal: Therefore their renown stands through the ages and their dynasties endured long.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore their fame endures through the ages and their dynasties lasted long.

sentences.zh: 昔我太祖高皇帝德範生民，功格天地，仰緯彤雲，俯臨紫極。

translations.literal: Of old our Grand Progenitor, the High Emperor, whose virtue patterned the living and whose merit reached Heaven and Earth, looked up to the crimson clouds and looked down upon the purple pole.
translations.idiomatic: Of old our Grand Progenitor, the High Emperor, whose virtue gave form to the people and whose merit reached Heaven and Earth, looked up to the crimson clouds and looked down upon the purple pole.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣興，增光前業，雲雨之所沾被，日月之所出入，莫不舉踵來王，交臂納貢。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent succeeded and enlarged the former enterprise; wherever rain and dew moistened and wherever sun and moon shone, none failed to lift their heels to come as kings or to offer tribute with folded arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent succeeded and enlarged the former enterprise; wherever rain and dew fell and wherever sun and moon shone, all came forward as vassals and offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 鬱林昏迷，顛覆厥序，俾我大齊之祚，翦焉將墜。

translations.literal: Emperor Yulin was benighted and overturned the proper order, so that the great fortune of our Great Qi was about to be cut down and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yulin was benighted and overturned the proper order, so that the great fortune of our Great Qi was about to fall.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝建道德之盛軌，垂仁義之至蹤，紹二祖之鴻基，繼三五之絕業。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, the Illustrious Emperor, established the supreme track of moral power and left the utmost traces of humaneness and righteousness, continuing the great foundation of the two founders and carrying on the interrupted work of the Three Dynasties and the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, the Illustrious Emperor, established the supreme way of moral power and left the utmost traces of humaneness and righteousness, continuing the foundation of the two founders and carrying on the work of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 昧旦丕顯，不明求衣，故奇士盈朝，異人輻湊。

translations.literal: From dawn he made great display and sought the unillumined as though he lacked clothes; therefore extraordinary men filled the court and unusual talents gathered like wheel spokes.
translations.idiomatic: He labored from dawn and sought what was still obscure as though he lacked clothes; extraordinary men filled the court and rare talents gathered like wheel spokes.

sentences.zh: 若迺經禮緯樂之文，定鼎作洛之制，非雲如醴之祥，白質黑章之瑞，諒以則天比大，無德稱焉。

translations.literal: As for the texts that regulate ritual and weave music, the institutions that fix the tripods and build Luoyang—if not omens like clouds shaped like yeast or the white quality and black pattern—surely they measured Heaven and matched greatness; none can be named without virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As for the texts regulating ritual and music, the institutions fixing the tripods and building Luoyang—if not omens like cloud-shaped yeast or white substance with black pattern—surely they matched Heaven in greatness; none can be named without virtue.

sentences.zh: 而嗣主不綱，窮肆陵暴，十諐畢行，三風咸襲。

translations.literal: Yet the successor lord lacked discipline and wildly indulged in arrogance and cruelty; the ten offenses were all committed and the three degeneracies all practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the successor lord lacked discipline and indulged in arrogance and cruelty; every grave offense was committed and every degeneracy practiced.

sentences.zh: 喪初而無哀貌，在慼而有喜容。

translations.literal: At the beginning of mourning he showed no grieving countenance; amid sorrow he wore a look of joy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of mourning he showed no grieving face; amid sorrow he wore a look of joy.

sentences.zh: 酣酒嗜音，罔懲其侮。

translations.literal: He drowned himself in wine and loved music and took no warning from their harm.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself in wine and loved music and took no warning from their harm.

sentences.zh: 讒賊狂邪，是與比周。

translations.literal: Slanderers, villains, the mad and the perverse were his intimates and companions.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers, villains, the mad and perverse were his intimates.

sentences.zh: 遂令親賢嬰荼毒之誅，宰輔受葅醢之戮。

translations.literal: Thus kinsmen dear and worthy suffered execution in bitter poison; leading ministers received slaughter like pickled meat.
translations.idiomatic: Thus worthy kinsmen suffered execution in bitter poison; leading ministers were slaughtered like meat for the pickle jar.

sentences.zh: 江僕射，蕭、劉領軍，徐司空，沈僕射，曹右衞，或外戚懿親，或皇室令德，或時宗民望，或國之虎臣，竝勳彰中興，功比申、邵，秉鈞贊契，受遺先朝。

translations.literal: Vice Director Jiang, the Xiao and Liu army commanders, Minister Xu, Vice Director Shen, and Cao of the Right Guard—whether maternal kin of honored relation, or men of imperial virtue, or pillars of the age and the people's hope, or tigers of the state—each had merit shining in the restoration and achievement comparable to Shen and Shao; they held the balance and aided the covenant and received the late emperor's trust.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang, the Xiao and Liu army commanders, Minister Xu, Vice Director Shen, and Cao of the Right Guard—whether maternal kin, men of imperial virtue, pillars of the age, or tigers of the state—each had merit in the restoration and achievement comparable to Shen and Shao; they held power, aided the covenant, and received the late emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 咸以名重見疑，正直貽斃，害加黨族，虐及嬰孺。

translations.literal: All because their fame made them suspect and their uprightness brought execution; harm reached their faction kin and cruelty extended even to infants.
translations.idiomatic: All were destroyed because their fame made them suspect and their uprightness brought execution; harm reached their clans and cruelty extended even to infants.

sentences.zh: 曾無《渭陽》追遠之情，不顧本枝殲落之痛。

translations.literal: Never a trace of the "Wei-yang" feeling of reaching back in kinship, nor heed for the pain of the withering of his own branch.
translations.idiomatic: He showed none of the kinship feeling of the "Wei-yang" ode, nor cared for the withering of his own house.

sentences.zh: 信必見疑，忠而獲罪，百姓業業，罔知攸暨。

translations.literal: Trust surely brings suspicion; loyalty yet wins guilt—the common people are fearful and know not where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Trust brings suspicion; loyalty wins guilt—the people are fearful and know not where to turn.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景內逼淫刑，外不堪命，驅土崩之民，爲免死之計，倒戈回刃，還指宮闕。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing, pressed within by licentious punishments and without unable to bear his office, drove a people already collapsing to a plan of escaping death; they turned spear and blade back and pointed at the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing, pressed within by licentious punishments and without unable to bear his post, drove a collapsing people to choose death over submission; they turned spear and blade back toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 城無完守，人有異圖。

translations.literal: The city had no complete defense; men's hearts held other designs.
translations.idiomatic: The city had no complete defense; men's hearts held other designs.

sentences.zh: 賴蕭令君勳濟宗祏，業拯蒼氓，四海蒙一匡之德，億兆憑再造之功。

translations.literal: Only through Lord Xiao's merit that rescued the ancestral temple and his enterprise that saved the black-haired people did the four seas receive the virtue of one restoration and the millions depend on the merit of a second creation.
translations.idiomatic: Only through Lord Xiao's merit that rescued the ancestral temple and his work that saved the people did the four seas receive the virtue of one restoration and the millions the blessing of a second creation.

sentences.zh: 江夏王拘迫威強，牽制巨力，迹屈當時，迺心可亮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia was constrained by overpowering force and harnessed by great pressure; his traces bent under the time, yet his inner heart could be made bright.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jiangxia was constrained by overpowering force; his outward conduct bent under the times, yet his inner heart could be made clear.

sentences.zh: 竟不能內恕探情，顯加鴆毒。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he could not inwardly forgive and probe feeling, but openly added poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he could not inwardly forgive and understand, but openly had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 蕭令君自以親惟族長，任實宗臣，至誡苦言，朝夕獻入，讒醜交構，漸見疏疑，浸潤成災，奄離怨酷。

translations.literal: Lord Xiao, considering himself the senior kinsman by kin and in truth a minister of the imperial clan, offered utmost admonition in bitter words morning and evening; slanderous vileness intertwined in plots, and he was gradually seen with suspicion; seeping slander became disaster and he was suddenly torn from bitter resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xiao, as senior kinsman and true minister of the clan, offered the sternest admonition morning and evening; slander intertwined in plots, suspicion grew, seeping calumny became disaster, and he was suddenly torn away in bitter death.

sentences.zh: 用人之功，以寧社稷，刈人之身，以騁淫濫。

translations.literal: He used men's achievement to settle the altars of state, yet cut down men's persons to indulge licentious excess.
translations.idiomatic: He used men's achievement to secure the altars of state, yet cut down men's lives to indulge his excesses.

sentences.zh: :　　台輔旣誅，姦小競用，梅蟲兒、茹法珍妖忍愚戾，窮縱醜惡，販鬻主威，以爲家勢，營惑嗣主，恣其妖虐。

translations.literal: : Once the terrace ministers were executed, base men vied for use; Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen were demonic, cruel, foolish and perverse, utterly indulging ugliness and evil, trafficking the ruler's authority to build family power, beguiling the successor lord and letting loose their demonic cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: : Once the leading ministers were executed, base men vied for power; Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen were demonic, cruel, foolish and perverse, trafficking the ruler's authority to build family power, beguiling the emperor and unleashing their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 宮女千餘，裸服宣婬，孽臣數十，袒裼相逐。

translations.literal: More than a thousand palace women in naked garments displayed licentiousness; several tens of wicked ministers in bare torsos chased one another.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand palace women in naked garments displayed licentiousness; dozens of wicked ministers with bare torsos chased one another.

sentences.zh: 帳飲闤肆之閒，宵遊街陌之上，提挈羣豎，以爲歡笑。

translations.literal: Between tent drinking and market stalls he wandered the streets at night, dragging groups of lads for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Between tent feasts and market stalls he wandered the streets at night, dragging bands of boys for his amusement.

sentences.zh: :　　劉山陽潛受凶旨，規肆狂逆，天誘其衷，卽就梟翦。

translations.literal: : Liu Shanyang secretly received murderous orders and plotted wild rebellion; Heaven guided his inmost heart and he was at once beheaded and cut down.
translations.idiomatic: : Liu Shanyang secretly received murderous orders and plotted treason; Heaven guided his heart and he was at once executed.

sentences.zh: :　　夫天生蒸民，樹之以君，使司牧之，勿使失性。

translations.literal: : Heaven generates the teeming people and sets up rulers for them, making them oversee and shepherd so they do not lose their nature.
translations.idiomatic: : Heaven generates the teeming people and sets up rulers to oversee and shepherd them so they do not lose their nature.

sentences.zh: 豈有尊臨宇縣，毒徧黔首，絕親戚之恩，無君臣之義，功重者先誅，勳高者速斃。

translations.literal: How can one who honorably faces All-under-Heaven spread poison through the black-haired people, cut off the grace of kin, lack the righteousness of ruler and minister, execute first those of heavy achievement, and swiftly put to death those of high merit?
translations.idiomatic: How can one who rules All-under-Heaven spread poison among the people, cut off kinship grace, destroy the bond between ruler and minister, execute first those of greatest merit, and swiftly kill those of highest achievement?

sentences.zh: 九族內離，四夷外叛，封境日蹙，戎馬交馳，帑藏旣空，百姓已竭，不卹不憂，慢遊是好。

translations.literal: The nine kin separate within, the four barbarians rebel without, the borders daily shrink, war-horses cross in charge, the treasury is already empty, the common people already exhausted—yet he shows no pity and no worry, but loves idle wandering.
translations.idiomatic: The nine degrees of kin turn against one another within, the four quarters rebel without, the borders shrink daily, war-horses clash, the treasury is empty, the people are exhausted—yet he shows no pity and loves only idle roaming.

sentences.zh: 民怨於下，天懲於上，故熒惑襲月，孽火燒宮，妖水表災，震蝕告沴。

translations.literal: The people resent below; Heaven punishes above—therefore Mars attacks the moon, baleful fire burns the palace, demonic water displays disaster, and quakes and eclipses proclaim omens.
translations.idiomatic: The people resent below and Heaven punishes above—Mars attacks the moon, baleful fire burns the palace, strange waters portend disaster, and earthquakes and eclipses proclaim ill omens.

sentences.zh: 七廟阽危，三才莫紀，大懼我四海之命，永淪于地。

translations.literal: The seven temples stand on the brink of peril; the three powers cannot be recorded—we greatly fear that the mandate of our four seas will forever sink into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: : The seven temples stand on the brink of ruin; heaven, earth, and man can no longer be ordered—we fear the mandate of the four seas may sink forever into the dust.

sentences.zh: :　　南康殿下體自高宗，天挺英懿。

translations.literal: : The Prince of Nankang, in person descended from Emperor Ming, was Heaven-endowed with heroic excellence.
translations.idiomatic: : The Prince of Nankang, in body descended from Emperor Ming, was endowed by Heaven with heroic excellence.

sentences.zh: 食葉之徵，著於弱年；

translations.literal: The omen of eating leaves was manifest in his weak years;
translations.idiomatic: The omen of eating leaves appeared in his tender years;

sentences.zh: 當璧之祥，兆乎綺歲。

translations.literal: the auspice of receiving the jade disk was foretold in his youthful years.
translations.idiomatic: the auspice of receiving the jade disk was foretold in his youthful years.

sentences.zh: 億兆顒顒，咸思戴奉。

translations.literal: The millions looked up with longing; all thought to uphold and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The millions looked up with longing; all wished to uphold and serve him.

sentences.zh: 且勢居上游，任總連帥，家國之否，寧濟是當。

translations.literal: Moreover his position lies in the upper stream and his charge gathers the linked commanders; when the house and state are in distress, it is for him to bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he holds the upper Yangzi and commands the linked governors; when house and state are in distress, on him rests the duty to bring peace.

sentences.zh: 莫府身備皇宗，忝荷顧託，憂深責重，誓清時難。

translations.literal: The headquarters, bearing the imperial clan, humbly bears entrusted care; grief is deep and responsibility heavy—we swear to clear the time's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: : The headquarters, as members of the imperial clan, humbly bear the entrusted charge; grief is deep and responsibility heavy—we swear to clear the age's calamity.

sentences.zh: 今命冠軍將軍、西中郎諮議、領中直兵參軍、軍主楊公則，寧朔將軍、領中兵參軍、軍主王法度，冠軍將軍、諮議參軍、軍主龐翽，輔國將軍、諮議參軍、領別駕、軍主宗夬，輔國將軍、諮議參軍、軍主樂藹等，領勁卒三萬，陵波電邁，逕造秣陵。

translations.literal: Now we order General of the Champion Yang Gongze, Adviser of the West Central Commandant and Commander of the Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; General of Pacifying the North Wang Fadu, Commander of the Central Army Aide, Army Commander; General of the Champion Pang Hui, Adviser Army Commander; General Who Assists the State Zong Jue, Adviser Army Commander and Assisting Officer, Army Commander; General Who Assists the State Yue Ai, Adviser Army Commander, and others to lead thirty thousand picked troops, crossing waves like lightning, and strike straight at Moling.
translations.idiomatic: : We now order Yang Gongze, General of the Champion, Adviser of the West Central Commandant and Commander of the Central Upright Army Aide; Wang Fadu, General of Pacifying the North and Commander of the Central Army Aide; Pang Hui, General of the Champion and Adviser Army Commander; Zong Jue, General Who Assists the State, Adviser Army Commander and Assisting Officer; Yue Ai, General Who Assists the State and Adviser Army Commander; and others to lead thirty thousand picked troops, swift as lightning over the waves, and march straight on Moling.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、領諮議、中直兵參軍、軍主蔡道恭，輔國將軍、中直兵參軍、右軍府司馬、軍主席闡文，輔國將軍、中直兵參軍、軍主任漾之，寧朔將軍、中直兵參軍、軍主韓孝仁，寧朔將軍、中直兵參軍、軍主朱斌，中直兵參軍、軍主宗冰之，建威將軍、中直兵參軍、軍主朱景舒，寧朔將軍、中直兵參軍、軍主庾域，寧遠將軍、軍主庾略等，被甲二萬，直指建業。

translations.literal: General of the Champion Cai Daogong, Concurrent Adviser and Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; General Who Assists the State Xi Chanwen, Central Upright Army Aide and Right Army headquarters Marshal, Army Commander; General Who Assists the State Ren Yangzhi, Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; General of Pacifying the North Han Xiaoren, Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; General of Pacifying the North Zhu Bin, Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; Central Upright Army Aide Zong Bingzhi, Army Commander; General Who Establishes Might Zhu Jingshu, Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; General of Pacifying the North Yu Yu, Central Upright Army Aide, Army Commander; General of Pacifying the Distance Yu Lue, Army Commander, and others—with twenty thousand in armor, strike straight at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: : Cai Daogong, General of the Champion, Concurrent Adviser and Central Upright Army Aide; Xi Chanwen, General Who Assists the State, Central Upright Army Aide and Right Army Marshal; Ren Yangzhi, General Who Assists the State and Central Upright Army Aide; Han Xiaoren and Zhu Bin, Generals of Pacifying the North and Central Upright Army Aides; Zong Bingzhi, Central Upright Army Aide; Zhu Jingshu, General Who Establishes Might and Central Upright Army Aide; Yu Yu, General of Pacifying the North and Central Upright Army Aide; Yu Lue, General of Pacifying the Distance; and others—with twenty thousand armored men, march straight on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍、武寧太守、軍主鄧元起，輔國將軍、前軍將軍、軍主王世興等，鐵騎一萬，分趨白下。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Deng Yuanqi, Administrator of Wuning, Army Commander; General Who Assists the State Wang Shixing, General of the Van, Army Commander, and others—with ten thousand iron cavalry, split and hurry toward Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: : Deng Yuanqi, General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Wuning; Wang Shixing, General Who Assists the State and General of the Van; and others—with ten thousand iron cavalry, split forces and hurry toward Baixia.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍、領司馬、新興太守夏侯詳，寧朔將軍、諮議參軍、軍主柳忱，寧朔將軍、領中兵參軍、軍主劉孝慶，建威將軍、軍主、江陵令江詮等，帥組甲五萬，駱驛繼發。

translations.literal: General Who Subdues the Barbarians Xiahou Xiang, Concurrent Marshal and Administrator of Xinxing; General of Pacifying the North Liu Qing, Adviser Army Commander; General of Pacifying the North Liu Xiaoqing, Commander of the Central Army Aide, Army Commander; General Who Establishes Might Jiang Quan, Army Commander and Magistrate of Jiangling, and others—command fifty thousand armored men in linked mail, dispatched relay upon relay.
translations.idiomatic: : Xiahou Xiang, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Concurrent Marshal and Administrator of Xinxing; Liu Qing, General of Pacifying the North and Adviser Army Commander; Liu Xiaoqing, General of Pacifying the North and Commander of the Central Army Aide; Jiang Quan, General Who Establishes Might, Army Commander and Magistrate of Jiangling; and others—lead fifty thousand men in mail, dispatched relay upon relay.

sentences.zh: 雄劔高麾，則五星從流；

translations.literal: When heroic swords are raised high, the five stars follow in stream;
translations.idiomatic: When heroic swords are raised on high, the five stars stream in their wake;

sentences.zh: 長戟遠指，則雲虹變色。

translations.literal: when long halberds point afar, clouds and rainbows change color.
translations.idiomatic: when long halberds point into the distance, clouds and rainbows change color.

sentences.zh: 天地爲之矞皇，山淵以之崩沸。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth thereby grow splendid; mountains and abysses thereby collapse and boil.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth grow splendid; mountains and abysses seem to collapse and boil.

sentences.zh: 莫府親貫甲冑，授律中權，董帥熊羆之士十有五萬，征鼓紛沓，雷動荊南。

translations.literal: The headquarters personally dons armor, sets law at the central balance, directs and leads a hundred fifty thousand warriors fierce as bear and pi, war drums in tumult, thunder rolling through southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: : The headquarters personally dons armor, sets law at the central helm, and directs a hundred and fifty thousand warriors fierce as bear and pi; war drums thunder through southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、南康王友蕭穎達領虎旅三萬，抗威後拒。
